title: The Silent Friend
content: Imagine your best friend is on the other side of the playground. You want to call them, but you can't shout! How will you tell them to come over? 🤔

title: Thinking Time!
content: Can you think of ways to talk to someone without using your voice? Try to wave your hand! What does waving mean?

content.title: Sending a Message
content.description: An animation showing a child waving to another child.

title: What is Communication?
content: When we share our thoughts, feelings, or information with someone, it is called **Communication**. We can talk, write, or even use our hands to communicate!

question: Which of these is a way of communicating?

title: Your Turn!
content: How did you communicate with your parents this morning? Did you say 'Good morning' or give them a hug?

title: Connecting the Dots
content: Just like we use words to talk, animals also communicate! Dogs bark, and birds chirp to talk to each other.

title: Let's Play a Game
content: Play a game of charades with your family. Try to act like an animal without making any sound, and let them guess!

title: The Distant Grandma
content: Your grandmother lives in another city. You want to show her your new drawing. How can you send it to her?

title: How does it reach?
content: If you put your drawing in a box, how does it magically travel to another city? Who takes it there?

content.title: The Journey of a Letter
content.description: A letter going into a red postbox, then traveling in a red van.

title: Means of Communication
content: We use things like **Letters**, **Telephones**, and **Computers** to talk to people who are far away. These are called Means of Communication.

question: What do we use to talk to someone far away?

title: Think About It
content: Have you ever spoken on a mobile phone? Who were you talking to?

title: Past and Present
content: A long time ago, people used pigeons to send letters! Today, we can send messages in a second using a mobile phone.

title: Paper Cup Phone
content: Take two paper cups and a long string. Ask an adult to make a hole in the bottom of each cup and tie the string. Now talk into one cup while your friend listens from the other. You made your own phone!
Encourage students to express themselves using non-verbal cues. Emphasize that listening is also a very important part of communication.
Students sometimes think communication only means speaking. Remind them that writing, drawing, and gestures are also communication.
